A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 18-page SFDATrack paper. Text, equations, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFDATrack benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses in Section 4, Tables 1–8, and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses in Section 4.

M1.justification: Equation (6) corrects the specified HPP assignment step by swapping the row and column normalization denominators. This revises the constraints used by Equation (7); the architecture and remaining objectives are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dark, Foggy, and Rainy variants of GOT-10k and DTB70, together with NAT2021, UAVDark70, and AVisT. Training domains, evaluation tasks, and attribute coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, the architectural comparison in Table 6, and Figures 4–5. No evaluated baseline is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Reported experimental settings remain identical, including 60,000 training samples, balanced 1:1:1 domain sampling, 300 epochs, ViT-Base, input sizes, and evaluation metrics. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Tables 4–8 retain the same component, alignment, architecture, loss-weight, and EMA-frequency ablations. The qualitative tracking examples and AVisT attribute analysis in Figures 4–5 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 changes SFDATrack's quoted AVisT AUC/precision from 59.64/58.25 to 60.87/59.70. Table 2 already reports 60.87/59.70 in v1 and remains unchanged in v2, so this resolves a textual inconsistency rather than demonstrating a performance gain. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (6) changes Q1_K=(1/K)1_N and Q^T1_N=(1/N)1_K to Q1_K=(1/N)1_N and Q^T1_N=(1/K)1_K. The corrected marginals both have total mass one; v1's totals were incompatible unless N=K. Other mathematical definitions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same source-free tracking contribution, DIM and HPP components, novelty claim, and claims of superior performance and weather generalization.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the ablations and generalization results are unchanged, including the second-best performance qualification for fog and sandstorm. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same software versions, hardware, architecture details, optimizer, learning rate, loss weights, and training information. The code-access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 56 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to source-dependent adaptive trackers and prior source-free adaptation research.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv version/date text is updated. Apart from the equation and numerical corrections assessed separately, the prose, terminology, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp on the first page is slightly repositioned and reformatted. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–8, their captions, and the body layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects incompatible assignment marginals in Equation (6) and reconciles Section 4.2's AVisT scores with the unchanged Table 2. These localized fixes improve mathematical correctness and internal consistency. The experimental evidence and scientific scope otherwise remain unchanged.
